label: conj:borromean-bloch-group-element
title: Borromean rings represent a non-trivial element of $K_3(\mathbb{C})$ / Bloch group with regulator $r_2 = 8G$
html:
Conjecture (K-theoretic / Bloch-group closure). The Borromean rings complement \mathbf{S}^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3 defines a non-trivial element [\mathcal{B}_3] \in K_3(\mathbb{C}) (equivalently, an element of the Bloch group B(\mathbb{C})) whose Beilinson regulator r_2: K_3(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R} evaluates to \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G. The Markov-trace coefficient h^4 = -3/4 of \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_3, q) has a K-theoretic shadow as the next-order regulator term: r_2[\mathcal{B}_3] \cdot (h^4\text{-coefficient}) = (8G)(-3/4) = -6G.

The K-theoretic structure

The Bloch group B(F) of a field F is generated by symbols [z] for z \in F \setminus \{0, 1\} modulo the 5-term relation

  [x] + [y] + [1 - xy] + \bigl[\tfrac{1 - x}{1 - xy}\bigr] + \bigl[\tfrac{1 - y}{1 - xy}\bigr]
  \;=\;
  0,

which IS the Bloch-Wigner / Rogers Pentagon identity for the dilogarithm. Bloch–Suslin showed B(\mathbb{C}) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong K_3^{\text{ind}}(\mathbb{C}) \otimes \mathbb{Q}.

The Beilinson regulator r_2: B(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R} is given by the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm:

  r_2([z]) \;=\; D(z)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \log|z| \cdot \arg(1 - z).

For an ideal tetrahedron with cross-ratio z = e^{i\theta} on the unit circle, \log|z| = 0, so the regulator collapses to the Clausen function

  D(e^{i\theta}) \;=\; \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}) \;=\; \mathrm{Cl}_2(\theta),
  \qquad
  \Lambda(\theta) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{Cl}_2(2\theta),

where \Lambda is the Lobachevsky function. So hyperbolic volume IS a regulator evaluation, per rem:vol-as-motivic-period. The two normalisations differ by both an argument doubling and a factor 2; keeping one function's coefficient while writing the other's name is a recurring slip.

The Borromean Bloch-group element

Per def:quantum-bloch-group and the classical Bloch-Suslin construction:

  • The Borromean complement decomposes into two regular ideal octahedra (Thurston), each of volume 4G = 4\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/2) \approx 3.66386.
  • In the Bloch group each octahedron is 4 \cdot [i], so the cross-ratio carried by the class is the fourth root of unity \zeta_4 = i = e^{i\pi/2} — not the sixth root e^{i\pi/3}, which is the figure-eight parameter.
  • The total Bloch-group element is
  [\mathcal{B}_3]_{B(\mathbb{C})}
  \;=\;
  8 \cdot [i]
  \;\in\;
  B(\mathbb{C}),

with regulator r_2[\mathcal{B}_3] = 8 \cdot D(i) = 8\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/2) = 8G (Catalan's constant; see prop:binding-scale-catalan). This is the \zeta_4 row of the transcendental-accounting table; the figure-eight sits in the \zeta_6 row with \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3).

The conjectural content — h^4 as the next-order regulator term

The Beilinson regulator extends to higher orders via the formal q-expansion of \Phi_q around q = 1 (the archimedean limit per conj:dilogarithm-archimedean-limit):

  \log \Phi_q(z)
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{q - 1}
  \bigl(
    \mathrm{Li}_2(z) + h \cdot R_1(z) + h^2 \cdot R_2(z) + \cdots
  \bigr),

where R_k(z) are higher-Bloch regulators. The conjecture is:

  \frac{r_2^{(2)}[\mathcal{B}_3]}{r_2[\mathcal{B}_3]}
  \;=\;
  h^4 \text{ coefficient of } \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_3, q)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{3}{4},

where r_2^{(2)} is the order-h^2 correction to the leading r_2 regulator. Equivalently: r_2^{(2)}[\mathcal{B}_3] = -6G.

Significance

Four candidate routes are open for deriving h^4 = -3/4 categorically:

  1. Direct Borromean Markov trace — already done
  2. Pachner-Pentagon state-sum — conj:pachner-pentagon-borromean
  3. K-theoretic / Bloch group regulator (this conjecture)
  4. DIM-master Pentagon — research-grade

Closing this conjecture ties h^4 to the K-theoretic structure of K_3(\mathbb{C}) — the deepest connection to motivic / arithmetic structure. It also closes the loop:

  • r_2 at order h^0 = 8G (the bare hyperbolic volume = production \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) in the canonical formalism),
  • r_2^{(2)} at order h^4 = -6G (the Markov-trace coefficient),
  • r_2^{(k)} at higher orders — the full Markov-trace closed form.

Structural invariants

  • GB filtration level: N/A — the Bloch group lives at the decategorified level (image of K_3(\mathbb{C}) in \mathbb{R}); no Coxeter length attaches naturally.
  • Jet order: h^4 (the load-bearing claim is at the next-order regulator level beyond the h^0 volume).
  • Bar-symmetry status: bar-symmetric. The Beilinson regulator r_2[z] = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \ldots is bar-symmetric under q \mapsto q^{-1} because \mathrm{Li}_2^q is bar-symmetric (per bar-involution.md Table 2 — Rogers q-dilog is bar-symmetric, Faddeev's \Phi_q alone is bar-anti- symmetric).

Lean axiomatisation (sketch)

class BorromeanBlochGroupElement
    (M : Type*) [BrCategory M] [QuantumDilogarithm M] where
  /-- The Bloch-group element of the Borromean complement. -/
  borromean_bloch_class : BlochGroup (Complex)
  /-- It equals 8 · [i], the ζ₄ (octahedral) class. -/
  borromean_bloch_eq_eight_xi :
    borromean_bloch_class = 8 • bloch_symbol Complex.I
  /-- The Beilinson regulator of the class equals 8G. -/
  regulator_eq_eight_G : r_2 borromean_bloch_class = 8 * catalan_G
  /-- The order-h² regulator correction equals -6G. -/
  regulator_h2_correction : r_2_h2_correction borromean_bloch_class = -6 * catalan_G
  /-- Equivalently, the h^4 Markov-trace coefficient = -3/4. -/
  borromean_h4_coefficient_from_regulator :
    markov_trace_h4_coefficient borromean_complement = -3/4

What remains open

  1. Compute prototype: at q = q_0, numerically evaluate both sides of the conjectural identity r_2^{(2)}[\mathcal{B}_3] = -6G. The left side requires extending the Bloch-Wigner regulator to order h^2 via the \Phi_q formal expansion; the right side is already in borromean-markov-trace-closed-form.md.
  2. Closing the conjecture needs an instance of the class above, and the borromean_h4_coefficient_from_regulator proof (which would import a Bloch-Suslin lemma from Mathlib once available; per lean_loogle search, K_3 formalisation is currently partial in Mathlib).
  3. Cross-validation. The Pachner–Pentagon state-sum and the K-theoretic regulator should both give h^4 = -3/4 — a triple cross-validation of the topological coefficient.
